**Why it works**
- Chrome on Android offers "Install" only if no installed app's scope covers the page's URL ([`isAppInstalledForUrl`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/chrome/android/java/src/org/chromium/chrome/browser/webapps/WebappRegistry.java)). A scope covers a URL whose path starts with the scope's path ([`IsUrlWithinScope`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/components/embedder_support/android/util/url_utilities.cc)).
- With `?goal=`, every goal's app had scope `/`, which covers every TallyBee URL. So once one goal was installed, Chrome treated every other goal as installed already.
- With `/alice/pushups/`, each goal's app has its own scope.
- **The Chrome catch:** Chrome 154–156 only checked whether any app from the site was installed, so no URL scheme helps there. The [fix](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/2e165cdb08d7) is in [Chrome 157](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8583262), which has been rolling out to Android since Nov 3.

**What's built**
1. A goal's URL is `tallybee.beeminder.com/alice/pushups/`. Without the final slash it still works, and the page adds the slash.
2. **Legacy redirect:** `?goal=pushups` still works and becomes `/alice/pushups/` once the goals load. Logged out, it stays as is until you log in, since the username isn't known yet.
3. **Hosting:** GitHub Pages has no file for a goal's URL, so it serves `404.html`, a byte-for-byte copy of `index.html`, with HTTP status 404.
   - Desktop Chrome reports no install problems with such a page.
   - `index.html` gained `<base href="/">`, so its files load from the root at any path.
   - **Cost:** after any edit to `index.html`, version bumps included, run `cp index.html 404.html`. A qual fails until you do.
4. **Login** still comes back to `/` and then goes on to the goal's URL. Beeminder only redirects to the exact URI registered for the app (`authorization.rb` in its oauth2-provider fork), so it can't come back to a goal's URL directly.
5. **Offline:** the service worker keeps whatever comes with a 404 as its copy of `404.html`. With no connection, it uses that for any URL it has no copy of, like GitHub Pages does.
